_note: Text for the landing page (/), in ASD-STE100. The hero shows the 3D mascot band (components/mascots-3d). Layout from the design canvas of issue #152 (duolingo.com hero, brilliant.org tutor and course tabs, a 4-step 'How it works' row). The project levels come from content/projects/.

meta.title: Jumper · Learn hardware on a 3D breadboard
meta.description: Connect real boards on a 3D breadboard. Jumper guides you like a game.

pitch.body: Build a desk robot that hears, talks and smiles, one glowing wire at a time. Real boards, a 3D breadboard, and no parts to buy.

wired.title: I have wired a board before
wired.body: Go straight to Perch, on the ESP32-S3

pitch.facts: {available} projects to play now · {soon} coming soon · parts from real kits

volt: Hi, I am Volt! I help you wire your first board.

band.label: Volt, Bulb, Knob and Coil, the four Jumper mascots, in 3D. Each mascot helps you in one project.
band.hint: Point at a mascot to make it cheer
band.hint_touch: Tap a mascot to make it cheer

tutor.body: Volt shows you each step on the board, tells you why, and helps when you are stuck. For the wiring, and for the code that runs on the board.

path.title: Level 3 · Ears
path.label: Perch: levels 1 and 2 are done, level 3 is next

code.title: Light an LED · Step by step
code.explain: Make the LED pin an output, so it can give power to the LED.

wiring.title: A guide on the board, not a manual
wiring.body: A pop-up on the 3D board tells you what to connect, where, and why. The correct holes glow.

wiring.title: Start at the right level
wiring.body: New to circuits? Start with Arduino Foundations. Wired before? Go straight to Perch.

wiring.title: Help when you are stuck
wiring.body: Watch a short clip of each level, or let Volt read the step aloud.

wiring.title: Know what to practice next
wiring.body: Your dashboard shows the mistakes that you make most, so you know what to do again.

codeCards.title: Write real Arduino code
codeCards.body: Type the sketch and press Run. The 3D board does what your code says.

codeCards.title: One line at a time
codeCards.body: Step by step mode explains each line in simple words before you type it.

codeCards.title: Code words
codeCards.body: Tap a word in the code to see what it means.

codeCards.title: Write it for me
codeCards.body: Stuck? Volt writes the sketch, and you still pass the level. Only the code XP is lost.

courses.title_start: From your first LED to a
courses.body: Each project is a real device, in short levels. Start with the basics, then build Perch.

parts.title: Real parts. Real pins.
parts.body: Each part is a model of a real part. The pins follow a published breadboard kit, so what you learn works on your desk.

steps.title: Make your first light turn on.
steps.body: Four steps. No parts. No soldering iron.

items.title: Pick your board
items.body: Start with an Arduino Uno and one LED, on a 3D breadboard.
items.alt: An Arduino Uno beside a breadboard in Jumper

items.title: Connect the pins
items.body: Volt tells you what to connect and why. The correct holes glow.
items.alt: A blue wire from pin 13 of the Uno to the resistor, and the LED on the breadboard

items.title: Press Check
items.body: Jumper checks each connection. A mistake tells you what to repair.
items.alt: The Check button and the message: All correct! The level is done.

items.title: Watch it come alive
items.body: Your LED turns on. Then Perch hears, talks and shows a face.
items.alt: Perch, the desk device, with a happy face on its screen
